title: Clinical features of systemic mastocytosis (SM)
tablehtml:
Presenting symptomsa {27060898; 34282774; 26809706; 11377686; 29048112; 33346151; 23991734; 24745681; 30545997; 28599188; 28599188; 34627355}

·   Constitutional symptoms (fatigue, weight loss, fever, diaphoresis)

·   Skin manifestations (pruritus, urticaria, dermatographia flushing)b

·   Mediator-related systemic events (abdominal pain, gastrointestinal distress, syncope, headache, hypotension, tachycardia, respiratory symptoms)c

·   Musculoskeletal symptoms (bone pain, osteopenia/osteoporosis, fractures, arthralgias, myalgias)

Clinical findingsd {27060898; 32108361; 26809706; 30545997; 28599188; 2643456; 1452127; 1617595; 16799608}

·   Lymphadenopathy

·   Hepatomegaly {2643456; 1452127; 1617595; 16799608}

·   Splenomegaly (often minimal)

Haematological abnormalities {27060898; 32108361; 26809706; 15307112; 31676322; 31509472; 28599188; 2128807; 24745679; 10909040}

·   Anaemia

·   Leukocytosis

·   Eosinophilia (a common finding)

·   Neutropenia and thrombocytopenia

·   Bone marrow failuree

·   Increased circulating mast cellsf

·   Associated haematological neoplasmg

Serum tryptase levels {27060898; 32108361; 34901755; 33346151; 26809706; 29048112}

·   > 20 ng/mLh

aThese disease manifestations can range in severity from mild to life-threatening. Symptoms related to organ impairment due to mast cell infiltration can also occur, in particular in patients with high-grade systemic mastocytosis (SM), including aggressive SM and mast cell leukaemia. bAbsent in bone marrow mastocytosis and indolent SM without skin lesions. Absence of skin lesions is often observed in advanced SM {34901755}. cSevere systemic symptoms can occur in patients with indolent SM as a result of extensive generation and release of biochemical mediators such as histamine, eicosanoids, proteases, and heparin. For example, gastrointestinal manifestations such as peptic ulcer disease and diarrhoea are more commonly attributed to the release of biologically active mediators than to infiltration of the gastrointestinal tract by excessive numbers of abnormal mast cells {24618605; 10909042}. dOrganomegaly is often absent in indolent SM but is usually present (along with impaired organ function) in advanced SM, including aggressive SM and mast cell leukaemia. eOccurs only in patients with aggressive or leukaemic disease variants. fSuggestive of mast cell leukaemia {28599188; 11377686}. gIn as many as 75% of SM cases, an associated haematological neoplasm (SM-AHN) is diagnosed before, simultaneously with, or after SM. In principle, any defined myeloid or lymphoid malignancy can occur with an associated haematological neoplasm, but myeloid neoplasms predominate, with chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia and myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable, being most common {2128807; 25025369; 15166264; 12363464; 11919425; 15160959}. In patients with SM-AHN, the clinical symptoms, disease course, and prognosis relate both to SM and to the associated haematological neoplasm {19363219; 11919425; 11377686}; in many cases, the clinical outcome is determined primarily by the associated haematological neoplasm {24262698; 14676628}. Therefore, both the type of SM and the type of associated haematological neoplasm should be classified according to the WHO criteria in all cases. hSerum total tryptase persistently > 20 ng/mL suggests SM and is a minor criterion for diagnosis {34901755; 11377686}. Because a number of other conditions are associated with an elevated tryptase level, the following restrictions should apply: (1) only the basal serum tryptase level (measured in a symptom-free interval) qualifies as a minor SM criterion; (2) the basal serum tryptase level does not qualify as a SM criterion when an associated haematological neoplasm is also diagnosed; and (3) in patients with known hereditary α-tryptasaemia, the basal tryptase level should be corrected accordingly.

title: Diagnostic criteria for systemic mastocytosis {34901755}
tablehtml:
Major criterion:

·   Multifocal dense infiltrates of mast cells (≥ 15 mast cells in aggregates) detected in sections of bone marrow and/or other extracutaneous organ(s)

Minor criteria:

·   Atypical mast cell morphology, including spindle shape or immature morphology, present in > 25% of all mast cells on bone marrow smears or in other extracutaneous organ(s)a

·   Mast cells aberrantly express one or more of the following antigens: CD2, CD25, CD30

·   KIT p.D816V mutation or other activating KIT mutationb detected in peripheral blood, bone marrow, or other extracutaneous organ(s)

·   Baseline serum tryptase concentration of > 20 ng/mL in the absence of an associated myeloid neoplasm; in the case of a known HαT, the tryptase level could be adjustedc

The diagnosis of systemic mastocytosis can be made if the major criterion and at least one minor criterion are fulfilled, or if at least three minor criteria are fulfilled.

HαT, hereditary α-tryptasaemia.

aWell-differentiated round cell morphology may be seen in a small subset of cases; mast cells in such cases are usually positive for CD30 and negative for CD2 and CD25. bAny type of KIT mutation counts as a minor systemic mastocytosis criterion when published solid evidence for its transforming behaviour is available (an overview of potentially activating KIT mutations is provided in the supplementary material of {34901755}). cA possible mode for adjustment has been proposed by Valent et al. (2021) {34901755}: the basal tryptase level may be divided by 1 plus the number of extra copies of the α-tryptase gene. For example, if the tryptase level is 30 ng/mL and two extra copies of the α-tryptase gene are found in a patient with HαT, the HαT-corrected tryptase level is 10 ng/mL (30/3 = 10), thereby not meeting the level of a minor systemic mastocytosis criterion.

title: Diagnostic criteria and morphological and molecular features for systemic mastocytosis (SM) subtypes {34901755}
tablehtml:
Subtype

Diagnostic criteria

Morphological features

Other features

Differential diagnoses

Bone marrow mastocytosis (BMM)

·   SM criteria fulfilled

·   No skin lesions

·   No B findingsa

·   Basal serum tryptase < 125 ng/mL

·   No dense SM infiltrates in an extramedullary organ

·   Low to very low MC burden in BM

·   Compact bone marrow MC infiltrates in > 70% of cases

·   Morphological features otherwise as in ISM

·   WD morphology rarely observed

·   In patients with WD morphology, mutation analysis in all other relevant regions of the KIT gene may be considered {25650093; 15070706; 26100086}

·   ISM without skin lesions

Indolent systemic mastocytosis (ISM)

·   SM criteria fulfilled

·   Typical skin lesions

·   At most one B findinga

·   ISM without skin lesions: at most one B findinga,b and/or basal serum tryptase ≥ 125 ng/mL and/or dense SM infiltrates in an extramedullary organ

·   Low MC burden in BM (usually < 5–10% of section area)

·   Compact MC infiltrates in > 70% of cases, typically of mixed morphology, containing numerous eosinophils, lymphocytes, fibroblasts, and histiocytes, in addition to neoplastic MCs

·   Usually > 25% spindle-shaped MCs

·   Haematopoiesis usually normal, mild reactive changes possible

·   Paratrabecular compact MC infiltrates often with prominent reticulin or collagen fibrosis and osteosclerotic changes in adjacent trabeculae

·   Atypical MCs in BM smears

·   WD morphology possible

·   KIT p.D816V mutation in 90–95%

·   In patients with WD morphology, mutation analysis in all other relevant regions of the KIT gene may be considered {25650093; 15070706; 26100086}

·   Cutaneous mastocytosis

·   SSM

·   ASM

Smouldering mastocytosis (SSM)

·   SM criteria fulfilled

·   At least two B findingsa

·   No C findingsa

·   High MC burden in the BM (usually > 30% of section area)

·   Diffuse-compact MC infiltration pattern

·   Usually spindle-shaped MCs embedded in a dense fibrotic stroma with pronounced osteosclerosis

·   Haematopoiesis often with mild dysplastic changes (not fulfilling WHO criteria for AHN)

·   WD morphology rarely observed

·   KIT p.D816V almost always present, usually with multilineage involvement

·   In patients with WD morphology, mutation analysis in all other relevant regions of the KIT gene may be considered {25650093; 15070706; 26100086}

·   High tryptase levels, organomegaly, and skin lesions in most cases

·   ISM

·   ASM

Aggressive systemic mastocytosis (ASM)

·   SM criteria fulfilled

·   At least one C findinga

·   High to very high MC burden in the BM

·   Diffuse-compact MC infiltration pattern

·   Usually spindle-shaped MCs embedded in a dense fibrotic stroma, occasionally with pronounced osteosclerosis

·   Pure ASM is less frequent than ASM-AHN

·   In BM smears, MCs > 5% and < 20% indicate ASM in transformation {24675021}

·   Haematopoiesis, often with mild dysplastic changes (not fulfilling WHO criteria for AHN)

·   WD morphology possible

·   KIT p.D816V almost always present, usually with multilineage involvement

·   In patients with WD morphology, mutation analysis in all other relevant regions of the KIT gene may be considered {25650093; 15070706; 26100086}

·   High tryptase levels

·   Skin lesions frequently absent

·   SSM

·   ASM-AHN

·   MCL

Systemic mastocytosis with an associated haematological neoplasm

(SM-AHN)

·   SM criteria fulfilled

·   Criteria for a WHO-defined haematological neoplasm; both disease compartments are classified according to WHO definitions

·   Any subtype of SM and any type of myeloid neoplasm can be detected, most frequently MDS/MPN (CMML), MDS, MPN, or AML

·   Morphology may encompass ASM or MCL, which would not be designated if an AHN diagnosis is established

·   WD morphology possible

·   KIT p.D816V usually present when sensitive techniques are applied

·   In patients with WD morphology, mutation analysis in all other relevant regions of the KIT gene may be considered {25650093; 15070706; 26100086}

·   Non-KIT mutations typically found in AHN

·   SSM

·   ASM

·   MCL

·   Tryptase-positive AML

·   Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia

Mast cell leukaemia (MCL)

·   SM criteria fulfilled

·   ≥ 20% MCs in BM smears

·   No AHN

·   In peripheral blood smears: ≥ 10% MCs in classic MCL, < 10% MCs in aleukaemic MCL

·   In acute MCL, C findings are detectable; chronic MCL (no C findings) has a much better prognosisa

·   High MC burden is common in BM

·   Diffuse-compact MC infiltration pattern

·   Predominantly round and hypogranulated MCs in most cases

·   Rarely, highly pleomorphic MCs with hypogranulation and cytoplasmic vacuolization

·   Reticulin content usually much lower than in SSM/ASM

·   WD morphology rarely observed (chronic MCL)

·   KIT p.D816V in ~50–70%

·   Other KIT codon 816 mutations, and mutations in other regions of KIT, are more frequent than in other SM subtypes

·   In patients with WD morphology, mutation analysis in all other relevant regions of the KIT gene may be considered {25650093; 15070706; 26100086}

·   Skin lesions absent in most patients

·   MCL-AHN

·   ASM

·   Tryptase-positive AML

·   Acute basophilic leukaemia

·   Monocytic leukaemias

title: Definitions of B findings (burden of disease) and C findings (cytoreduction required) {34901755}
source:
Table 5 (B- and C-findings): the table is the same with Table 5 in the recent paper published in HemaSphere and Table 3.04 in the 4th edition of the WHO Handbook.

Ian: It appears that the 4th edition came first, so again, should be OK
tablehtml:
B findings:

·      High mast cell burden: Infiltration in bone marrow ≥ 30% and/or serum tryptase ≥ 200 ng/mLa and/or KIT p.D816V variant allele frequency (VAF) ≥ 10% in bone marrow or peripheral blood leukocytes

·      Signs of myeloproliferation and/or myelodysplasia not fulfilling criteria for AHNb

·      Hepatomegaly on palpation or imaging (ultrasound, CT, or MRI) without ascites or other signs of organ damage and/or splenomegaly on palpation or imaging without hypersplenism and/or lymphadenopathy on palpation or imaging (> 20 mm)

C findings:

·      Cytopenia(s) (one or more found):

o   Absolute neutrophil count < 1 × 109/L

o   Haemoglobin < 10 g/dL

o   Platelet count < 1.0 × 109/L

·      Hepatopathy: Ascites and elevated liver enzymesc ± hepatomegaly or cirrhotic liver ± portal hypertension

·      Spleen: Palpable splenomegaly with hypersplenism ± weight loss ± hypoalbuminaemia

·      Gastrointestinal tract: Malabsorption with hypoalbuminaemia ± weight loss

·      Bone: Large-sized osteolysis (≥ 20 mm) ± pathological fracture ± bone pain

AHN, associated haematological neoplasm; MDS, myelodysplastic neoplasm; MDS/MPN, myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm; MPN, myeloproliferative neoplasm; SM, systemic mastocytosis; SM-AHN, systemic mastocytosis with an associated haematological neoplasm.

aIn the case of a known hereditary α-tryptasaemia (HαT), the basal serum tryptase level can be adjusted. The optimal method of adjustment is not definitively defined. A common method is to divide the basal tryptase level by 1 plus the number of extra copies of the α-tryptase gene. For example, with a tryptase level of 300 and two extra copies of the α-tryptase gene in a patient with HαT, the HαT-corrected tryptase level is 100 (300/3 = 100) and therefore does not qualify as a B finding. bSigns of myeloproliferation and/or myelodysplasia must be discrete and stable and must not meet diagnostic criteria for an MPN, MDS, or MDS/MPN, excluding SM-AHN. The presence of a myeloid AHN excludes B findings and smouldering systemic mastocytosis by definition. cAlkaline phosphatase levels are typically elevated in patients with advanced SM and SM-induced liver damage. In some of these patients, only elevated liver enzymes are found, without (clinically relevant) ascites.
